items.title: Godfrey Hirsch Interview, 1987-10-27
items.q: Dave Winston, uh, Dave Jacobson, the fiddle player, Harry Burke, he couldn't get over there during the day.

ctx.x: You ought to see his son. He looks just like him. Is that right? I've seen the picture.

I didn't know his son. How about the Tulaneans? The Tulaneans? Yeah. Well that was a group of guys from the Tulane band. Right. But it was a jazz band. It was a jazz band. We played at the Strand Theater for a week. Uh huh. We had a dancer, a cheerleader dancer, something like that. We were on the stage there for a week. I'll never forget it was the week that we played LSU. What year are we talking about? I left in 27. Must have been in 27. Strand Theater. Yes. Who was in the band? You got me naming so damn many…

items.title: Godfrey Hirsch Interview, 1987-10-20
items.q: This is when we went, Harry Burke and I went to the World's Fair in 33.

ctx.x: I thought that picture would be in here. This is when we went, Harry Burke and I went to the World's Fair in 33. This is Notre Dame University and this is, these are pictures taken along the road. Who was Harry Burke? Harry Burke was a piano player and an accordion player. More or less a teacher than he was a musician. This is for digging instruments, digging vibes and all. This is me. Really? Yeah, you don't recognize it.
Well you do look a little bit.
